signalling.text: The D2 receptor couples to Gi/o proteins, inhibiting adenylyl cyclase and reducing neuronal excitability and dopamine release at terminals.

claim.text: D2 receptors are densely expressed in the dorsal and ventral striatum, where antipsychotic blockade produces both therapeutic response and extrapyramidal or prolactin effects.

signalling.text: The 5-HT2A receptor couples to Gq/11, activating phospholipase C and increasing cortical pyramidal excitability.

claim.text: 5-HT2A receptors are richly expressed across prefrontal cortex, where second-generation antipsychotics block them alongside D2.

signalling.text: The M1 receptor couples to Gq/11 and is concentrated postsynaptically in cortex and hippocampus, supporting memory and cognition.

claim.text: M1 receptors predominate in cortex and hippocampus; selective M1 activation is pursued for cognitive symptoms with fewer peripheral effects.

signalling.text: The M4 receptor couples to Gi/o and acts largely as an inhibitory autoreceptor and striatal modulator of dopamine release.

claim.text: M4 receptors in the striatum restrain dopamine release, which is the rationale for M4-preferring agonism in psychosis.

signalling.text: GluN2A is a regulatory subunit of the NMDA glutamate receptor, a calcium-permeable coincidence detector central to synaptic plasticity.

claim.text: GluN2A-containing NMDA receptors are prominent in hippocampus and cortex, including on parvalbumin interneurons implicated in the glutamate model of psychosis.

signalling.text: The 5-HT1A receptor couples to Gi/o and acts as a presynaptic autoreceptor in raphe and as a postsynaptic heteroreceptor in cortex and hippocampus, lowering neuronal firing when activated.

claim.text: 5-HT1A receptors are dense in prefrontal and hippocampal cortex and on raphe neurons, where partial agonism can raise 5-HT release from raphe while dampening cortical 5-HT1A-mediated effects.

signalling.text: SERT is the presynaptic reuptake carrier for serotonin; inhibiting it raises and prolongs serotonin in the synaptic cleft, and is the shared mechanism of most antidepressants used in mood and anxiety disorders.

claim.text: SERT is expressed along the raphe projections and in prefrontal and limbic cortex; the raphe itself is not resolved in the atlas so the midbrain and pons stand in as a schematic anchor.

signalling.text: The 5-HT2C receptor couples to Gq/11 and is a widespread inhibitory heteroreceptor in midbrain and cortex, modulating monoamine release and feeding behaviour.

claim.text: 5-HT2C receptors in midbrain and cortico-striatal circuits are implicated in appetite and metabolic effects of antipsychotic and antidepressant drugs.

signalling.text: The H1 receptor couples to Gq and is widely expressed in cortex and thalamus, promoting wakefulness and arousal.

claim.text: H1 blockade is the shared mechanism behind sedation and appetite increase across tricyclic, mirtazapine, and sedating antipsychotic drugs.

signalling.text: The alpha-2A adrenergic receptor couples to Gi/o and acts as an inhibitory presynaptic autoreceptor on noradrenergic and serotonergic terminals.

claim.text: Alpha-2A agonism in the locus coeruleus and cortex reduces noradrenaline release and is the main mechanism of mirtazapine's antidepressant and sedative action.

signalling.text: The alpha-1A receptor couples to Gq and mediates excitatory postsynaptic noradrenergic transmission, including vascular smooth muscle contraction.

claim.text: Alpha-1A blockade lowers standing blood pressure and is the main orthostatic and urinary source of adverse effects for tricyclics, mirtazapine and antipsychotics.

signalling.text: GluA1 is the principal postsynaptic subunit of AMPA receptors, which mediate the fast excitatory transmission required for synaptic plasticity and learning.

claim.text: GluA1-containing AMPA receptors dominate cortico-hippocampal excitatory transmission, and rapid-acting antidepressants such as ketamine increase GluA1 signalling on inhibitory interneurons.

signalling.text: TrkB is the receptor for brain-derived neurotrophic factor and couples to MAPK and PI3K signalling, regulating neuronal survival, growth and synaptic plasticity.

claim.text: BDNF-TrkB signalling in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex supports the neuroplasticity hypothesis of depression, with BDNF pathway genes enriched in large GWAS of depression.

signalling.text: The M2 receptor couples to Gi/o and serves as an inhibitory presynaptic autoreceptor in cholinergic terminals, limiting acetylcholine release.

claim.text: Cholinergic M2 autoreceptors in cortex, hippocampus and amygdala modulate limbic circuitry implicated in mood regulation, and cholinergic anti-muscarinic activity contributes to cognitive adverse effects.

signalling.text: TAAR1 is an intracellular Gs-coupled receptor on monoaminergic neurons that modulates dopamine, serotonin and norepinephrine release, and is activated by amphetamines and trace amines.

claim.text: TAAR1 agonism was developed as a schizophrenia and mood therapy, though the large DIAMOND phase 3 trials in schizophrenia failed to meet their primary endpoint.
